headline: Competing model undercuts OpenAI pricing by 11x, reshaping AI economics
body: A new model called BDH-CQ is pricing AI tasks at $0.007 each, undercutting OpenAI's Luna offering even when Luna is discounted 80%. This cost differential signals a tightening AI vendor landscape where price competition is intensifying alongside OpenAI's reported $40B revenue run rate. For healthcare systems evaluating AI deployment for clinical workflows and EHR integration, this pricing pressure creates negotiating leverage and forces vendors to justify costs against emerging alternatives. The economics matter significantly in value-based care models where margins are thin and technology ROI directly impacts profitability. Healthcare consultants should expect clients to demand more aggressive vendor pricing as cost-competitive models mature and proliferate.
